title: Thermal Regime and Active Layer Deepening in the Schirmacher Oasis: Five Decades of Ground Temperature Evolution in Queen Maud Land
abstract: Ground temperature time-series collected across twelve boreholes in the ice-free Schirmacher Oasis reveal sustained active layer expansion at a rate of 0.84 cm/year over the 2010–2023 observation interval. Surface warming trends are most pronounced in late austral summer, accompanied by enhanced suprapermafrost subsurface flow draining toward Lake Priyadarshini.

title: Aerosol Optical Properties and Radiative Forcing of Marine Air Masses over Coastal East Antarctica Observed from Bharati Station
abstract: We present two full years of continuous aerosol scattering, absorption, and optical depth measurements from India's Bharati Station in Larsemann Hills. Marine biogenic sulfur emissions during peak austral summer enhance fine-mode aerosol fractions, exerting a net top-of-atmosphere cooling radiative forcing of -1.4 ± 0.3 W/m².

title: Sustained In-Situ Moored Observations (IndARC) Reveal Winter Warming and Atlantic Water Pulses in Kongsfjorden, Svalbard
abstract: Moored oceanographic time series from India's IndARC observatory in high-latitude Kongsfjorden capture unprecedented mid-winter episodic intrusions of transformed Atlantic Water. Heat flux anomalies correspond with anomalous negative phases of the North Atlantic Oscillation, establishing empirical constraints for circumpolar sea ice loss teleconnections.

title: Decadal Mass Deficit and Ice Dynamics of Sutri Dhaka Glacier in Chandra Basin, Western Himalaya
abstract: Continuous glaciological field monitoring and Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) surveys at Sutri Dhaka Glacier reveal a mean cumulative negative mass balance of -0.68 ± 0.12 m w.e. a⁻¹ between 2013 and 2023. Runoff simulations project a 22% increase in peak summer discharge by 2040, followed by severe post-monsoon baseflow decline.

title: Cold-Active Lipases from Novel Psychrotolerant Arthrobacter Isolated from Antarctic Lake Priyadarshini
journal: Extremophiles: Microbial Life Under Extreme Conditions
abstract: We report the isolation, genomic sequencing, and enzyme characterization of a novel psychrotrophic bacterium Arthrobacter sp. strain ANT-Priyadarshini-04 from benthic algal mats of Lake Priyadarshini, Schirmacher Oasis. The cloned lipase maintains 78% of maximum catalytic velocity at 4°C, presenting exceptional promise for cold-water bioprocessing.

title: Air-Sea Carbon Fluxes and Water Mass Modification across the Polar Frontal Zone in the Indian Sector of the Southern Ocean
journal: Deep Sea Research Part II: Topical Studies in Oceanography
abstract: Underway carbon dioxide partial pressure (pCO2) and biogeochemical transects between 40°S and 67°S reveal intense biological carbon drawdown in the Polar Frontal Zone during late austral summer, moderating Southern Ocean oceanic CO2 uptake.
